title: Cortical mastoidectomy
text: Cortical mastoidectomy, canal wall up. In this film we follow the operation step by step on a three dimensional model of a right temporal bone, and watch the mastoid being drilled away layer by layer, to reach the antrum while protecting the facial nerve, the labyrinth, the sigmoid sinus and the dura.

title: Indications and imaging
text: The operation is done for acute mastoiditis that does not settle on antibiotics, or for chronic otitis media with cholesteatoma. A C T of the temporal bones shows the extent of the disease and of pneumatisation, and warns of a low tegmen, a forward lying sigmoid sinus, a fistula of the lateral canal, or dehiscence of the facial canal.

title: Position and incision
text: The patient lies supine with the head turned away, and the facial nerve is monitored. A postauricular incision is made about one centimetre behind the crease, from the top of the auricle down to the mastoid tip. In small children it is placed higher and more posteriorly.

title: Expose the cortex
text: A musculoperiosteal flap is raised and the auricle is pushed forwards. The landmarks on the cortex are identified: the spine of Henle, the suprameatal, or MacEwen's, triangle, the temporal line, and the mastoid tip.

title: Saucerise the mastoid
text: With a large cutting burr and suction irrigation, drilling starts at MacEwen's triangle, along the temporal line, which marks the level of the tegmen, and parallel to the posterior canal wall. The cavity is kept wide and saucer shaped, rather than a deep hole.

title: Tegmen and sigmoid sinus
text: The bone is thinned over the middle fossa dura above, and over the sigmoid sinus behind, with the sinodural angle between them. These define the upper and posterior limits of the dissection.

title: Open the antrum
text: About one and a half centimetres deep, beneath MacEwen's triangle, the antrum opens. Körner's septum can masquerade as its medial wall. Pus, granulation tissue or cholesteatoma is removed.

title: Lateral canal and incus
text: On the medial wall of the antrum lies the smooth, hard bulge of the lateral semicircular canal. In front of it, through the aditus, the short process of the incus sits in the fossa incudis. The burr must never touch the incus.

title: Find the facial nerve
text: The second genu of the facial nerve lies below the lateral canal and medial to the short process of the incus. The mastoid segment runs down, medial to the posterior canal wall, to the stylomastoid foramen at the front of the digastric ridge. The bone over it is thinned with a diamond burr and copious irrigation. The facial recess, between the nerve and the chorda tympani, is opened if access to the middle ear is needed.

title: Close and after care
text: Facial nerve function is checked before waking, the wound is closed in layers, and a mastoid dressing is applied. Facial movement is tested on recovery, and hearing and balance afterwards.

title: Structures at risk
text: To summarise, the structures at risk are the facial nerve, the lateral semicircular canal and the labyrinth, the sigmoid sinus, the incus, the chorda tympani, and the tegmen with the middle fossa dura. This film is for education only. Always check surgical detail against current atlases and senior guidance.
